ECE 6390 / Waves and fields

Displacement current

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how magnetic circulation remains consistent across a charging capacitor gap.

Ampère–Maxwell law includes conduction current and changing electric displacement: ∮H·dl = Icond + d/dt∫D·dA. The changing gap flux supplies the term that connects the two circuit sides.

For circular plates of radius R and uniform changing field, a concentric loop encloses Ienc = I min(1, r²/R²). Symmetry gives H = Ienc/(2πr), in A/m.

Inside the plate radius, enclosed current grows as r² and H grows as r. Outside, the enclosed current is constant and H falls as 1/r. The idealization neglects fringing and transient propagation details.

Example

A loop at r = R/2 encloses one quarter of the changing flux and displacement current. Its magnetic field magnitude is one half of H at r = R.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. Why does applying H = I/(2πr) with the full wire current fail for a loop smaller than the plate radius?

    The smaller spanning surface encloses only part of the uniform changing electric flux.

    Its enclosed displacement current is I(r/R)². Using the full current would overstate magnetic circulation; the correct field inside is Ir/(2πR²).
